test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 30 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two trains start from stations A and B and travel towards each other at the speeds of 60 km/h and 70 km/h respectively. At the time of their meeting, the second train has travelled 100 km more than the first. The distance between A and B is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The difference in **speeds** is 70 − 60 = 10 km/h.

This difference causes a lead of **100 km** for the faster train.

Time taken to meet = Distance difference ÷ Speed difference = 100 ÷ 10 = **10 hours**.

Total distance = (Sum of speeds) × Time = (60 + 70) × 10 = 1300 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 1300 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Train 1 (S₁) = **60 km/h**

Speed of Train 2 (S₂) = **70 km/h**

Difference in distance = **100 km**

**Formula:** Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac5ac23a63a534cdaa2b7d8f316d30c0ff078035160b4dcce42f8ddd86bde556.png] 

⇒ Let the time taken to meet be **t** hours.

⇒ Distance covered by the first train (d₁) = 60 × t

⇒ Distance covered by the second train (d₂) = 70 × t

⇒ According to the problem: d₂ − d₁ = 100

⇒ 70t − 60t = 100

⇒ 10t = 100 ⇒ t = 10 hours

⇒ Total distance between A and B = d₁ + d₂ = 60t + 70t

⇒ Total Distance = 130t = 130 × 10 = 1300 km

**∴ The correct answer is 1300 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the **difference** between their individual speeds (|S₁ − S₂|).

Meeting Time Formula

Time of Meeting = Initial Distance between objects ÷ Relative Speed.

Distance Proportion

Since Time is constant until the meeting point, the **Ratio of Distance** covered is equal to the **Ratio of Speeds** (D₁/D₂ = S₁/S₂).

**∴ The correct answer is 1300 km.**</p
